title: The Iron(ic) Melting Pot: Reviewing Human Evaluation in Humour, Irony and Sarcasm Generation

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying 17 NLG research papers to assess the reporting rate of human evaluator language proficiency, and discussing the overwhelming bias towards the English language in NLP research.

Surveying 17 NLG papers to measure the percentage that report the location or nationality of their human evaluators, highlighting how cultural and regional differences impact the interpretation of humor, irony, and sarcasm.
Surveying 17 NLG papers to calculate the proportion that report evaluator age, noting age-related differences in the ability to correctly perceive intended sarcasm.

Surveying 17 NLG papers to find the percentage that report evaluator gender, pointing out the historical and ongoing bias toward male-dominated participant samples in computer science and its effect on humor perception.

Surveying 17 NLG papers to determine how often evaluator education and social class are reported, emphasizing the overrepresentation of WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialised, Rich, Democratic) populations due to heavy reliance on crowdsourcing platforms.
